newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Wider U.S. trade gap seen hurting Q3 GDP.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Wider U.S. trade gap seen hurting Q3 GDP.

text.p: The September U.S. trade data dealt third-quarter gross domestic product a surprise left to the chin Wednesday morning, prompting lower GDP forecasts from economists in a Reuters poll.
On average, the 24 experts said last quarter's GDP growth would come in closer to a 1.8 percent annual rate than the Commerce Department's previous estimate of 2.2 percent.
Although most pundits already were counting on a slight downward revision to GDP, they said the trade report pushed them to lower their GDP forecasts another 0.2 to 0.3 percent.
The U.S. trade deficit widened 10.1 percent in September to $11.34 billion, the Commerce Department said on Wednesday.
"Net exports is going to be a bit more of a drag than what was estimated intitially," said Chris Iggo, chief economist at BZW Securities Inc. "Inventories might be a little bit lower as well."
Exports declined 1.4 percent in September to $69.78 billion, while imports grew 0.1 percent to $80.13 billion.

"Frankly, people don't know where these imports are, because they're not in inventories and they don't appear to be in the consumer spending numbers," said Gail Fosler, chief economist at the Conference Board.

In September, business inventories, one component of GDP, rose a slight 0.1 percent, Commerce said last Friday. Analysts said the small increase resulted from a drop in wholesale inventories, which fell 1.28 percent.
The trade report did not seem to affect economists' projections for fourth-quarter GDP. On average, 23 experts said GDP would rebound to 2.4 percent.
"Trade took a lot out of Q3 ... (but) it would have to keep going up a lot to take a lot out of Q4," said Stuart Hoffman, chief economist at PNC Bank Corp.
